strategies.summary: Classify the day by which kill zone first taps the higher-timeframe PD array and displaces away from it. If London does it, expect a London-made extreme and a New York retracement or continuation; if London misses, expect New York to tap the array and reverse.

timeframes.notes: Bias comes from the presenter's higher-timeframe PD array read on 1h, 4h or 1d; the profile itself is classified on 15m as Asia, London and New York interact with that array. Session-dependent rules need intraday data because session windows and NY-time opens are not usable from 1d candles.

glossary.Classic Daily Profile: Asia consolidates, London taps the higher-timeframe array and creates the daily extreme, then New York retraces and continues from that London move.
glossary.New York Reversal: Asia and London fail to tap the higher-timeframe array, so New York reaches it, creates the daily extreme, and reverses the prior intraday direction.
glossary.London Close: 10:00 to 12:00 New York time; in this lesson it is mainly a profit-taking window rather than a fresh continuation entry session.

custom_signals.name: htf_pd_array_tap
custom_signals.plain_definition: Price trades into a higher-timeframe discount array (bullish) or premium array (bearish), such as a fair value gap or order block.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (low <= bullish_fvg[0].gap_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_fvg[0].gap_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_fvg[0].filled@bias_tf) OR (low <= bullish_ob[0].zone_high@bias_tf AND high >= bullish_ob[0].zone_low@bias_tf AND NOT bullish_ob[0].invalidated@bias_tf)

custom_signals.name: displacement_candle
custom_signals.plain_definition: A strong expansion candle in the trade direction.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: close > open AND body >= K_DISPLACEMENT_BODY_MULT * avg(body[-1], K_DISPLACEMENT_LOOKBACK)

custom_signals.name: prior_session_expansion
custom_signals.plain_definition: An earlier session in the same New York day already displaced in the trade direction and left at least one fair value gap, so the next session is less likely to fully retrace and sweep it.
custom_signals.numeric_definition: (kill_zone == london AND count(bullish_fvg[0].formed AND ny_minute >= 20:00, ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1) OR (kill_zone == new_york_am AND count(bullish_fvg[0].formed AND (ny_minute >= 20:00 OR ny_minute < 07:00), ny_minute / tf_minutes + 240 / tf_minutes + 1) >= 1)

custom_signals.name: pre_major_news
custom_signals.plain_definition: The part of a CPI, FOMC or NFP release day before the release time.

custom_signals.name: htf_opposing_pd_array
custom_signals.plain_definition: The opposing higher-timeframe premium array (for longs) that acts as the draw on liquidity.

sequence: Mark the higher-timeframe PD array that fits the directional idea for the day.
Watch the 15m Asia, London and New York sessions to see which one first trades into that array and displaces away from it.
If London does it, treat London as the daily extreme and look for New York to retrace and continue that move.
If London misses and New York does it, treat New York as the reversal session and the daily extreme.
Take profit into the opposing higher-timeframe liquidity objective and avoid new continuation entries during London close.

invalidation.text: If a session already has a strong expansion leaving FVGs, do not expect the next session to fully retrace and sweep its extreme.

filters.text: Do not take new continuation entries during the London Close session; it is meant for taking profit.
The economic calendar supersedes rigid session profiles; volatility is required for the intended move.
You must adapt to which session taps the HTF array; do not blindly assume London will make the high/low of the day.

entry_rule.text: Enter in New York on the retracement after London creates the extreme, or in New York on the reversal after New York itself taps the higher-timeframe array.
entry_rule.quote: you have to get involved right here in New York and this was a very very clean setup actually

target_rule.text: Target the opposing higher-timeframe liquidity pool or opposing premium/discount array.
target_rule.quote: it means that London close will take profit it will take profit at what at a liquidity Point

stop_rule.text: Place the stop beyond the high or low of the session that actually tapped the higher-timeframe array and made the daily extreme.
stop_rule.quote: that was my entry covering the high and then aiming for new lows

management.notes: Take full profit during the London Close or when the HTF target is reached.

strategies.notes: Context framework, not a standalone entry model: the lesson decides which session should make the high or low of the day, then expects the actual execution pattern to come from another entry model. The higher-timeframe bias is the presenter's PD-array read, not Traidle's BOS/CHoCH structure bias; the key adaptation is to stop assuming London must make the extreme and instead follow the session that actually taps the array.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price taps into a Daily fair value gap during the Asian session.
The Asian session expands lower immediately, leaving bearish fair value gaps.
Because Asia already displaced, London lacks the energy to fully retrace or sweep Asia. Instead, London forms a shallow retracement.
New York session begins, taps into the retracement, and provides the actual continuation setup lower.

examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter stresses that trading killzones requires reaction, not rigid adherence to a template. Because the Australian Dollar is active during Asia, it caused the primary displacement. Consequently, expecting London to sweep Asia was illogical; the trader had to adapt and enter the continuation during New York.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Asia forms a range. London expands, sweeping both Asia lows and Asia highs, but does not reach the overhead daily fair value gap.
Because London failed to tap the HTF array, the trader anticipates New York will complete the objective.
New York session opens, rallies into the daily fair value gap, creates the high of the day, and immediately displaces lower.
A short entry is taken during the New York expansion, placing the stop loss above the newly formed NY high of the day.

examples.presenter_commentary: He emphasizes that predicting a New York reversal wasn't based on Asia consolidating, but entirely on the fact that London failed to tap the daily FVG. The session that taps the HTF array dictates the true daily extreme.
